To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
behavioral contrast and sensitivity of response ratios in multiple schedules are not influenced by regular or irregular alternations of components.
the predictability of reinforcement in time does not affect behavioral contrast, response-ratio sensitivity, or response-ratio sensitivity of response ratios.

(1) contrast and sensitivity of ratios of response rates to reinforcer ratios were not affected by the manner of alternation of components and (2) the magnitude of contrast depended on the ratio of reinforcer rates, not on the absolute rate.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effects of the predictability of reinforcement in multiple-schedule performance, with the predictability of the time of reinforcement, as well as with the predictability in the sense of regularity of the schedule.
the effects of regularity in time of future events on performance.
the role of temporal regularities in the control of behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the regularity or irregularity of component alternation is not an important variable in the performance of multiple schedules.
the manner in which multiple-schedule components are alternated does not affect the magnitude of behavioral contrast or response ratios.
the regularity or predictability of reinforcement in a multiple schedule is not an important factor affecting performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the regular alternation of reinforcement conditions in multiple schedules does not affect the magnitude of behavioral contrast, the response-ratio function, or the sensitivity of response ratios.
multiple-schedule performance is not affected by whether or not component alternation is regular.

the effects of multiple schedules are not determined by the predictability of reinforcement conditions, but rather by the predictability in space of reinforcement conditions, that is, by the regularity of reinforcement schedules.
The main takeaway from our work is that
behavioral contrast is a robust phenomenon in multiple schedules, and that the manner in which component durations are arranged does not affect its occurrence.
the regularity in the schedule of reinforcement is not necessary for the occurrence of behavioral contrast.
behavioral contrast and undermatching occur regardless of whether the schedule is a regular multiple schedule or a random multiple schedule.
